title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The Decision of the AI Office outlines the official stance and guidelines adopted by the AI Office regarding AI development and deployment. It includes key principles, operational procedures, and compliance expectations that stakeholders must follow.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy outlines how the organization will recruit and staff technology specialists in artificial intelligence, detailing the qualifications, roles, and responsibilities required for these positions. It also establishes guidelines for ensuring that hiring practices align with the organization’s broader AI strategy and compliance standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The AI Office is announcing a vacancy for a Lead Scientific Adviser. The document would outline the duties, qualifications, and application procedure for interested candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy explains how to fill a legal officer position in the AI Office, detailing required qualifications, duties, and the application process. It also outlines the legal responsibilities of the role, ensuring compliance with AI regulations and company standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy outlines how to fill open AI‑policy officer roles, detailing the qualifications needed and the steps for selecting suitable candidates. It also sets expectations for the duties and accountability of these officers once they are appointed.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts created to advise the European Union on how to regulate artificial intelligence. They gather evidence, analyze technical risks, and recommend rules that aim to keep AI safe and trustworthy while encouraging innovation.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This policy proposes a request to establish standard guidelines for developing, deploying, and using artificial intelligence. It aims to ensure consistency, safety, and transparency across AI systems by setting common technical and ethical standards.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The “CoP Consultation Notice” announces that a consultation is being held on a Community of Practice initiative. It invites stakeholders to review the proposed plans and provide feedback on the direction and scope of the community.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This policy invites individuals or organizations to express interest in forming a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI policy. It outlines the process for submitting expressions of interest and highlights the objectives and benefits of participation.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This document provides a visual guide to the iterative drafting process used in the CoP. It shows how ideas are developed, reviewed, and refined through multiple cycles of drafting and feedback.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document presents a graphic timeline illustrating the drafting process for the Community of Practice policy. It outlines the sequence of stages, key dates, and milestones involved in developing and finalizing the policy.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document outlines an initial set of guidelines for responsible AI use, serving as a draft framework for organizations to develop and implement AI practices. It aims to provide a starting point for establishing consistent, ethical AI standards within a given community or industry.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The "Code of Practice: 2nd Draft" is a set of guidelines aimed at helping organizations implement and manage artificial intelligence responsibly. It outlines best practices for design, deployment, and oversight to ensure ethical, safe, and effective use of AI technologies.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document outlines guidelines and best practices for developing, deploying, and governing AI systems to ensure safety, fairness, and transparency. It updates earlier versions with new recommendations and clarifies the responsibilities of developers, users, and regulators.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed agreement aimed at guiding the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It sets out principles like transparency, fairness, and accountability to help shape how AI systems are designed, deployed, and governed.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final establishes a worldwide agreement for the safe, ethical, and responsible development and deployment of AI technologies, calling for transparency, accountability, and cooperation among governments, industry, and civil society. It commits participants to protect privacy, mitigate bias, promote equitable access, and align AI innovations with human values and shared global benefits.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy lists AI activities that are forbidden, such as producing deceptive or manipulative content, misusing personal data without consent, and using AI to aid illegal or harmful actions. It aims to ensure that AI is developed and used ethically by clearly setting out what is not allowed.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy explains how organizations should identify and classify artificial intelligence systems within their operations. It provides clear criteria and definitions for what counts as an AI system, helping to ensure consistency in reporting and compliance.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines how the organization will communicate strategies to support start‑ups and foster innovation. It highlights key initiatives, partnerships, and messaging intended to attract talent, investment, and collaboration across the innovation ecosystem.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program designed to help early‑stage companies access high‑performance computing resources and expertise. By offering training, technical support, and computing credits, it aims to accelerate innovation and growth in the European HPC ecosystem.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This slideshow webinar focuses on risk management principles, guiding participants through identifying, evaluating, and mitigating risks in various contexts. It aims to equip viewers with practical strategies to protect projects, organizations, and stakeholders from uncertainty and potential harm.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar discusses how to manage and mitigate risks related to AI deployments. It covers best practices and strategies for identifying, assessing, and controlling potential AI‑related hazards.
